title: Scheduled Node Retirement & Rolling Maintenance Automation
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Implement an automated node lifecycle controller for Dedicated fleets that manages scheduled maintenance windows, graceful draining, phased upgrades, and planned node retirements while preserving throughput guarantees and interacting safely with autoscaling policies.
acceptance_criteria: A controller exists that can schedule maintenance windows per-fleet and per-availability-zone
Nodes enter a cordon->drain->upgrade->rejoin lifecycle without manual intervention for planned events
Autoscaler respects in-flight drains and can temporarily inject reserved capacity to maintain throughput SLOs
Console UI shows maintenance windows and current node lifecycle state; operators can manually pause/resume or force-finish
Rollbacks automatically trigger when health checks fail on >X% of nodes in a batch and surface an incident with remediation steps
We observe <=2% sustained capacity reduction during a rolling maintenance of up to 30% of fleet nodes
proposed_solution: Build a Fleet Lifecycle Controller (FLC) as a control-plane component. The FLC exposes APIs to create maintenance windows and retirement schedules. For each scheduled event the FLC: 1) computes a safe drain batch size based on current throughput targets and active autoscaler headroom; 2) updates node state to CORDON and starts health-aware drain procedures (evicting sessions, warming fallback pools); 3) requests temporary burst capacity or leverages reserved pools if drain threatens throughput SLOs; 4) performs upgrade/retirement actions and verifies post-upgrade health; 5) uncordons nodes and marks lifecycle complete. Integrations: autoscaler, serving runtime health API, Console for scheduling and visibility, audit log/KMS for approvals. Use optimistic locking and idempotent transitions to avoid double-actions. Local agent on node will coordinate KV cache preservation/warmup and report progress to FLC.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal infra dev cluster - schedule small maintenance windows on non-critical pools (1 week)
Beta: 5% of Dedicated fleets in staging that mirror customer workloads (2 cycles)
Canary: 1 production customer bucket with traffic guard rails and manual on-call standby (2 maintenance windows)
Gradual ramp to 25% fleets with monitoring thresholds gating each increase
Full rollout after 4 successful canary cycles and SLO verification
implementation_notes: Controller persisted in our control-plane DB with optimistic concurrency keys
Drain behavior: prefer connection draining over abrupt termination; configurable grace period per fleet
Autoscaler integration: endpoint to request temporary reserve tokens and specify budgeted burst hours
Node agent responsibilities: accept CORDON/UNCORDON, run pre-drain hooks (dump KV cache snapshot), post-upgrade warmup
Use feature flag gating for multi-AZ rolling vs single-AZ to iterate safely
Add extensive telemetry: per-drain latency, eviction counts, model-inference tail latency during drains
risks: Insufficient capacity during simultaneous scheduled events across AZs could violate throughput guarantees
Race between autoscaler scaling down and FLC drain may cause nodes to be removed mid-drain
Upgrades that change kernel/kernel-rt behavior could expose regressions requiring rollback
Operator UI misuse could schedule overlapping windows unintentionally without proper validation
Complexity of KV cache preservation across node retirement might increase restore time
metrics: planned_drain_success_rate: % of drains completing within SLA
